slides.title: The Plan Turns Mapping Into a Schedule
bullets: A concrete translation of segmentation and mapping into activity
Specifies which expert, at what cadence, through what interaction
Without a plan, segmentation is just an analysis exercise

slides.title: Sustained Scientific Partnership
bullets: Multi-year cadence, not a fixed number of annual visits
Advisory boards and trial-design or evidence-generation discussions
Strategic scientific dialogue that goes beyond a single product

slides.title: Translation Support and Relationship-Building
bullets: Tier 2 centers on helping contextualise global evidence locally
Tier 2 interactions can be more frequent but less strategically deep
Tier 3 prioritises relationship-building and disease education
Tier 3 nurtures rising stars and clinical champions long-term

slides.title: What a Good Plan Actually Specifies
bullets: The objective of each interaction: education, insight, evidence, advisory
The appropriate channel: visit, congress, call, advisory board, digital
What success looks like for the expert, not only for the company

slides.title: Plans Need Built-In Flexibility
bullets: A rising star or shifting institution can move tiers quickly
Good plans are revisited, commonly quarterly
Not fixed for a full year on a twelve-month-old assessment

slides.title: From Strategy to Daily Discipline
bullets: Connects segmentation and mapping to territory ownership
Turns knowing who matters into a concrete daily action plan

takeaway.title: The engagement plan turns segmentation and mapping into a concrete schedule of action
bullets: Each tier needs a distinct cadence, channel and objective
A good plan defines success for the expert, not just the company
Plans require quarterly flexibility as expert influence shifts
